# AIPOCH

> AIPOCH develops AIPOCH Open-Science, an open-source, local-first AI research workbench with portable .science packages, and reusable scientific agent skills.

## Primary Pages

- [AIPOCH Homepage](https://aipoch.com/): Overview of the research workbench, scientific skills ecosystem, evaluation framework, documentation, and product updates.
- [AIPOCH Open-Science](https://aipoch.com/open-science): Product overview covering scientific agents, Python and R execution, scientific Connectors, traceable artifacts, model choice, and portable .science packages.
- [AIPOCH Open-Science Downloads](https://aipoch.com/open-science/download): Current stable installers, supported operating systems, installation requirements, release information, and update guidance for the desktop application.
- [AIPOCH Open-Science Documentation](https://aipoch.com/docs/): Maintained guides for installation, projects, models, tools, permissions, execution, research records, and sharing workflows.
- [AIPOCH Open-Science Documentation Index for AI Assistants](https://aipoch.com/docs/llms.txt): Official documentation index with direct page links and summaries for installation, research workflows, tools, permissions, and .science packages.
- [AIPOCH Open-Science Source Code](https://github.com/aipoch/open-science): Official Apache-2.0 source repository with implementation details, contribution guidance, issue tracking, and release history.
- [Latest AIPOCH Open-Science Release](https://github.com/aipoch/open-science/releases/latest): Latest published release notes, installation assets, fixes, compatibility information, and version-specific changes.

## .science Packages and Research Evidence

- [.science Package Guide](https://aipoch.com/docs/guides/research-packages/): Export selected research records, inspect a read-only import, create a writable fork, and understand included contents and transfer boundaries.
- [AIPOCH Open-Science .science Package Overview](https://aipoch.com/blog/aipoch-open-science-research-packages): Explains why portable research records matter and how .science packages support review, handoff, and continued work.
- [AIPOCH Open-Science Use Cases](https://aipoch.com/open-science/use-cases): Browse research cases showing questions, connected workflows, inspectable outputs, and selected .science packages; individual cases have their own scope.
- [AIPOCH Open-Science Preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.17110): Research preprint describing the .science exchange contract, controlled tests, preservation of recorded relationships, and interpretation limits.
- [AIPOCH Open-Science Preprint Overview](https://aipoch.com/blog/aipoch-open-science-preprint): Accessible introduction to the paper, its research-record design, evaluation methods, illustrated examples, and reported limitations.

## Setup and Research Workflows

- [Installation and Updates](https://aipoch.com/docs/guides/installation/): Platform-specific installation instructions, prerequisites, updates, and troubleshooting entry points for supported desktop systems.
- [First-Time Setup](https://aipoch.com/docs/guides/onboarding/): Set up the workspace, select supported model access, and prepare the environment needed for research tasks.
- [Your First Project and Result](https://aipoch.com/docs/guides/first-project/): Worked introduction to creating a project, providing inputs, requesting research work, and inspecting saved outputs.
- [Notebook and Execution Evidence](https://aipoch.com/docs/guides/notebook/): Use Notebook execution and inspect recorded code, runtime information, results, and evidence associated with research outputs.
- [Reproducibility](https://aipoch.com/docs/guides/reproducibility/): Understand artifact-version checks, evidence requirements, execution conditions, and the distinction between recorded checks and new verification.
- [Permissions and Approvals](https://aipoch.com/docs/guides/approval-modes/): Configure conversation approval modes, inspect remembered permissions, manage grants, and understand their effective scope and limitations.
- [Models and Task Policies](https://aipoch.com/docs/guides/models/): Configure model-related task policies and understand how model selection affects research operations and application features.

## Skills, Specialists, and Evaluation

- [Medical Research Agent Skills](https://aipoch.com/agent-skills): Overview of the medical research skills ecosystem, supported integrations, installation methods, and research workflow categories.
- [Scientific Skills Library](https://aipoch.com/agent-skills/list): Searchable website catalog of medical and scientific methods; this catalog is distinct from the desktop application's bundled resources.
- [Skill Marketplace Guide](https://aipoch.com/docs/skills/marketplace/): Browse and install additional Skills, inspect resource details, and understand the marketplace workflow in the application.
- [Specialists](https://aipoch.com/docs/specialists/overview/): Configure focused agent roles, assign capabilities, delegate scoped tasks, and review results within the researcher's permissions.
- [AIPOCH Open-Science Benchmarks](https://aipoch.com/benchmark/open-science): Self-reported AstaBench and ASI-Bench results, with methods, task scopes, model configurations, and limits on cross-split and public-leaderboard comparisons.
- [MedSkillAudit](https://aipoch.com/benchmark/medskillaudit): Evaluation framework explaining research-skill checks, veto gates, scoring methodology, supporting evidence, and release-readiness decisions.
- [Skill Leaderboard](https://aipoch.com/leaderboard): Published skill evaluation results, scores, and category filters; evaluation scores are not clinical certification or universal performance guarantees.

## Resources

- [AIPOCH Blog](https://aipoch.com/blog): Product announcements, release notes, architecture explanations, research workflows, and practical tutorials, each with its own date and version scope.
- [What Is AIPOCH Open-Science?](https://aipoch.com/blog/what-is-open-science): Introduction to the workbench, project organization, agents, execution, artifacts, provenance, and model choice; check the article's stated version scope.

## Key Facts and Boundaries

- AIPOCH Open-Science is AIPOCH's open-source AI research workbench. The product name is distinct from the broader open science movement.
- The desktop application is distributed under the Apache License 2.0 and supports macOS, Windows, and Linux. External models, services, and compute may charge separately.
- Projects, sessions, files, settings, and artifacts are stored locally by default. Local-first does not mean every workflow is offline.
- Configured external models, searches, remote Connectors, MCP services, and compute hosts may receive task context, arguments, or files. Active permissions and receiving-service policies govern these operations.
- Model availability depends on the account, provider, agent backend, API protocol, region, and installed application version.
- A .science package can carry selected conversation branches, file versions, Notebook records, and verification evidence for review, handoff, and archiving. Included files depend on export selection.
- Side Chat conversations, private reading bookmarks, and their notes are excluded from .science packages. Exported materials still require review before sharing.
- Imported research history is read-only. Importing or browsing it does not execute code, restore credentials, or transfer permission grants.
- Continuing from imported history requires a separate writable fork and appropriate receiving-side model, runtime, and permission settings; code does not run automatically.
- Received verification records describe the sender's checks. They do not prove that the receiving computer reran those checks or that every research conclusion is scientifically valid.
- The linked arXiv paper is a preprint reporting an exchange design and scoped tests. It is not peer-review approval or evidence of universal validation.
- Built-in Skills, marketplace Skills, Specialists, Connectors, and website catalog entries are different resource sets. Counts vary by release and catalog scope and are not automatically additive.
- Reviewer findings, provenance records, MedSkillAudit results, and examples support inspection and review; researchers remain responsible for methods, data governance, interpretation, and scientific validation.
- Download pages and release notes describe current distribution details. Guides, articles, papers, and cases may document a specific version or controlled scenario.
